title: /v1/demos sends signed webhook events from committed state, retried with back-off and given up after 8 attempts
steps: S1: With TEST_DATABASE_URL set to a disposable PostgreSQL server, run run.cmd.
S2: Confirm every test named in run.tests reports ok.
expect: signatureHeader('whsec_dGVzdC12ZWN0b3Itc2VjcmV0', the vector body, 1762905600) is t=1762905600,v1=dd23e53f0c15ffa6949b481e57089c164c817cfcdbbac38b9954d5d70d2c4d19 (openssl dgst -sha256 -hmac gives the same hex).

PUT /v1/demos/webhook refuses 422 INVALID_WEBHOOK_URL with errors [{path: url, code}]: HTTPS_REQUIRED for http, CREDENTIALS_NOT_ALLOWED, PORT_NOT_ALLOWED, PRIVATE_ADDRESS for 127.0.0.1, 10/8, 169.254.169.254, ::1, fe80::1, localhost and a host resolving to a private address; nothing is kept.

A valid PUT answers the secret (whsec_ + 43 characters) once; the row keeps it sealed; GET never answers it; a replacing PUT makes a new secret and keeps since; DELETE answers removed true, then false.

The sweep makes demo.accepted, demo.completed (with site.shareUrl), demo.failed (error.code) and demo.opened (one per counted open) once each, only for demos accepted after registration, never for a cancelled demo or a rolled-back status; the body is {id, type, createdAt, demo} with demo equal to GET /v1/demos/:id.

Delivery POSTs with redirect manual, an AbortSignal, X-Tracy-Event-Id and the signature; 500, a network error, a timeout and a 302 retry after 30 s tripling; 204 delivers and is never sent again; the 8th failed attempt gives up; a replaced address receives pending events signed with its new secret; a removed address gives them up unsent.

tests: the signature is the hex HMAC-SHA256 of "<t>.<body>" keyed with the whole secret
a webhook address is https, on the default port, without credentials, on a public host
register, read and remove: the secret is answered once and kept sealed; the token decides the account
each event of a demo accepted after registration is made once, from committed state, with the demo as GET answers it
delivery: a signed POST, 2xx delivers; a failure waits and retries; the 8th failure, or no address, gives up
the sweep makes then sends in one tick, one tick at a time, and keeps old settled events a month
